zoe: Quick sync — wrapping up Experiment-3 for per-cardset max_tokens tuning across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. Found one surprising regression on H100 when the kernel selector flipped to the 'fused-kv-sparse' path.

arjun: Curious — is that regression latency or throughput?

zoe: Primarily p95 latency for short-chat workloads (seq len ~64). p50 fine, p95 jumps ~18%. Throughput drops ~6% at target QPS.

casey: Do you have the profile traces? might be kv-cache fragmentation or kernel warmup.

zoe: Pushed a couple of traces to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/job-2856789/h100/trace-1/*. Flame shows hot on small matmul kernel after KV fetch.

perf-bot: Perf run completed: 2856789-exp3-h100 — p50: 12ms (+1ms), p95: 78ms (+12ms), tokens/s: -6% 

lee: Hmm. Could be a kernel selector heuristic that prefers larger GEMM tiling when token budget is high, but our per-batch max_tokens here dropped KV reuse efficiency, so more KV miss churn.

samir: Related config we ran: ```yaml
batching:
  max_tokens_per_batch:
    H100: 76800
    A100: 51200
    A10: 24576
    L4: 20480
    T4: 16384
  queue_policy: age_based
  token_budget_target: 0.85
```

arjun: Can we try two quick forks: (A) lower H100 max_tokens to 60000, keep kernel selection as-is; (B) same max_tokens=76800 but force kernel_selector: prefer-kv-friendly for small sequences.

zoe: Already ran A and B yesterday. A reduced p95 regression to +4% (still slightly worse than baseline), B removed the regression but throughput dropped more (-9%). Logs show B triggered a different kernel that has higher per-token overhead.

casey: That suggests a tradeoff: kernel that favors KV locality is heavier per-token. For short seqs, latency matters. For long seqs, it pays off. We need dynamic policy per seq-length distribution.

lee: Agree. Could implement kernel selection override per slice based on estimated seq length, or use quick heuristic at queue front: if avg_seq_len < 128 prefer low-latency kernel, else kv-friendly.

samir: One more wrinkle: our KV cache fragmentation metric spiked when batch packing was aggressive. When we cap max_tokens, packing becomes denser and fragments KV shards differently on H100 due to our sharding algorithm.

zoe: Good point. I dumped kv_shard_utilization for the failing run: many shards ~80% used but several near-empty causing imbalance. That increases cross-shard syncs.

arjun: Proposal: add a small anti-fragmentation step in packer: prefer pack layouts that keep per-shard token variance under 25%. It's a cheap heuristic.

casey: Let's also add quick experiment: run the same configs but with "packing_bias: shard_balance" toggle. If that reduces p95 without affecting tokens/s then win.

perf-bot: Scheduled experiments: 2856790000-A (H100 max_tokens=60000), 2856790100-B (force-kernel=kv-friendly), 2856790200-C (packing_bias=shard_balance). Results ETA in ~2h.

zoe: For the rollout plan: if C reduces p95 < 5% delta and tokens/s >= -3% we can enable packing_bias by default on H100 and A100. Else fallback to per-length kernel override.

lee: One more test: try lowering token_budget_target from 0.85 -> 0.75 to see if lowering burst aggressiveness avoids fragmentation. Could be cheaper than changing kernel selection.

samir: I'll queue that as D. 2856790300-D (token_budget=0.75).

zoe: Thanks. I'll collect all traces and write a short runbook for eng-runtime with recommended defaults per cardclass after these runs.

arjun: SGTM. Also add a note about measuring KV shard imbalance in the console dashboard so we have live alerts.

casey: :+1:

zoe: OK wrapping — will post summary thread with numbers and config diffs once perf-bot finishes. Thanks team.
